title: What If a Whole Thunderstorm Became One Giant Raindrop?
description: AI-narrated science commentary: a fun 'what if' thought experiment about combining every raindrop in a storm into one giant drop, and why real physics won't let it happen. Original commentary, not a repost.

beats.text: What if every raindrop in a single thunderstorm fused into one giant drop?
A big storm can dump over a billion gallons of water on a city in under an hour.
Physics says that mega-drop couldn't even survive as a sphere -- surface tension can't hold something that big together.
beats.broll_query: water droplet surface tension macro slow motion

beats.text: It would shred apart in mid-air, breaking into smaller droplets before it ever reached the ground.
beats.broll_query: raindrop breaking apart high speed camera

beats.text: That's actually why real raindrops max out around a centimeter wide -- anything bigger just splits apart mid-fall.
beats.broll_query: close up raindrop falling slow motion

beats.text: So the mega-drop storm makes a great thought experiment, but the atmosphere itself won't allow it.
